reason: The mark stays on its line. Four rules move together, and every one of them is about what happens where the tool meets the paper. First, the wander is measured in stroke widths instead of the figure's representative size: at 8% of a radius a thin pencil left its own line by eleven widths on a large arc while a small one stayed on it, so `AMPLITUDE_WIDTHS` -- fine 0.35, medium 0.6, broad 2.0, the middle value ruled by the author on 2026-08-09 from sheets drawn at 0.6 and 0.9 -- multiplies the stroke width, and the clamp at 0.40 of the representative size stays as the safety valve for a figure smaller than its own mark. Second, the material outline is taken from the performed ink rather than the intended geometry, for every work and not only for `wild`: the median distance from a decoration vertex to the ink band falls from 16.09, 5.99, 8.11 and 6.09 px on a large arc, a small arc, a circle and a square to 3.21, 2.26, 3.07 and 2.80. Third, the fray is no longer a `stroke-dasharray`; the stroke is drawn only where a contact field over the paper crosses a threshold, so among 192 fragments of a sample sheet one pair shares a length and 2.6% fall on a multiple of the sampling step, while the proportion of a stroke that touches at all is still read per tool from the old dash table. Fourth, two rules fit the tone to the tool: a stratum is never wider than 0.33 of the tool's nominal mark -- nominal, because paper tooth and powder do not get finer because the line was drawn finer, which is what `test_material_outline_absolute_widths_do_not_move` holds -- and a stratum's centre is never inside the actual mark. Of the 549 cases frozen for engine 27, 454 move and 95 do not; the 95 are every case drawn with the five tools that carry no material outline (rotring 22, drypoint 21, silverpoint 19, computer 17, burin 16). The blur, the motion energy that injects the wander, `FREQUENCY_CYCLES` and the group path are untouched.
